newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH will have to pay premium to UK firms-analysts.
newsitem.headline: LVMH will have to pay premium to UK firms-analysts.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH will have to pay British merger partners Guinness and Grand Metropolitan Plc a premium if it wants a drinks merger in which it would be the leading shareholder with 35 percent, analysts said.
Several estimated the premium at around five billion francs, or less if LVMH agrees to give up the 60 pence a share payout proposed by the British groups to their shareholders.
They estimate the payout to LVMH, the biggest shareholder in both groups with 14.2 percent of Guinness and 6.4 percent of GrandMet, at 2.4 billion francs.

The British companies announced plans to merge in May despite the opposition of LVMH, which has brought strong pressure to bear on them by going to court and by building a stake in GrandMet and courting its shareholders.
It wants to create a drinks group combining their spirits and wine activities and proposes a de-merger of their other activities -- fast foods, beer and canned goods.

But analysts say the assets brought to the drinks group by LVMH, its Guinness and GrandMet stakes and 66 percent of its drinks subsidiary Moet Hennessy are worth around 45 billion francs, only around 30 percent of the value of the three companies' spirits and wines businesses.

LVMH declined to comment on the analysts' estimates or the British groups' reactions. They said LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault's plan would be costly and complicated and would give him control without his having to pay for it.

Analysts say GrandMet's board appears more receptive than Guinness to Arnault's plan. "The GrandMet people are very open to discussions because they aren't saddled with a past with Bernard Arnault as has Guinness chairman Tony Greener," said one share analyst.
"It's a complicated debate because this is neither a friendly merger nor a hostile takeover bid. It's a semi-hostile merger complicated by parities and the choices of assets," said another analyst.
